item.title: England thrashed by Australia in first ODI to provide welcome distraction to sandpaper scandal
item.description: England crashed to a heavy defeat in the first game of their latest Australian tour, with a rousing debut from 21-year-old Mahli Beardman diverting some of the home side’s attention from the ongoing sandpaper scandal . Australian cricket is in the midst of a bitter civil war over Usman Khawaja’s historic ball-tampering allegations but the hosts still eased to a seven-wicket victory in in the first ODI in Perth , where local boy Beardman collected stunning figures of six for 24. It proved another calamitous visit to Optus Stadium for England, who thew away the first Ashes Test in two days on the same ground 12 months ago. With Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood all rested between Test series, Australia pieced together an inexperienced attack and watched as it dismantled their rivals. At one stage England were 65 for eight and staring at a record low total, with some late repair work by the tail lifting them to 131 all out. Travis Head missed the chance to repeat his match-winning Ashes knock when he was bowled cheaply by Gus Atkinson but skipper Mitch Marsh took up the mantle, clubbing 50 off just 30 balls to lead a chase that was all over in less than 24 overs. England were criticised last winter for being too casual in their preparations Down Under but that has not been the case this time. They have trained hard, given themselves time to acclimatise and beaten Western Australia in a warm-up game at the WACA. All of that work came to nothing, though, as they followed up a disappointing tri-series in Pakistan with a fourth loss in their last five outings. After being sent in England’s openers scraped together 24 before Australia bagged their first, Ben Duckett slashing Spencer Johnson to backward point. Ben Duckett was the first English batsman to get out (AP) Tom Banton came closer than anyone to finding form, hitting five fours on his way to 25 before driving with hard hands at the tidy Xavier Bartlett. An average start then transformed into a dreadful once as the introduction of Beardman plunged the innings into turmoil. Kicking off his senior international career with England’s two best batters at the crease, the youngster got the best of both. His eighth ball was sharp and well directed, with enough swing to take the outside edge as Harry Brook went back in defence. Joe Root , on the day he became just the third Englishman to 200 ODI appearances, was even bigger scalp. Muddling his way to 17 from 36 balls, he was put down by Cooper Connolly on three before an optimistic drive off Beardman wound up in Josh Inglis’ gloves. The celebrations showed how much that wicket meant but he was just warming up. Jordan Cox followed to another defensive nick and Beardman showed his range by bouncing out Sam Curran , who hooked obligingly to fine leg for a seven-ball duck. item.title: Bears Stadium Bids Flood In As Developers Push City Plan
item.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Developers are flooding the market with unsolicited bids to keep the Chicago Bears in the city, but the team’s focus remains on a suburban deal or a move to Indiana. This bid arrives as the Bears prepare for a legislative session in Illinois starting Nov. 17, yet the franchise has not endorsed any of these urban proposals. The group plans to span about 100 acres and include a stadium for 75,000 fans alongside thousands of new homes. They argue that an urban site offers better economic value than remote suburbs. “It is our belief that a modern, competitive dome stadium such as the one that we are proposing will outperform suburban locations such as Arlington Heights or northwest Indiana,” said Quintin Primo III, founder and executive chairman of Capri Investment Group, during a news conference in Bronzeville, according to Yahoo . Local leaders back the idea, but the NFL has previously flagged the specific Reese parcel as too narrow with active rail lines running through it. City Dreams Versus Team Reality While local boosters push for a downtown solution, the Bears are actively exploring a path across the state line. Nearly nine months ago, Indiana state leaders approved a funding package, and due diligence has been completed regarding two potential locations in Hammond. The team has not commented on the specific Chicago proposals but is watching the Illinois political process closely. “We expect productive dialogue with both leadership teams in the coming weeks,” the Bears said last week regarding the two states, according to Yahoo Sports . The franchise is seeking property tax certainty and infrastructure help, with its main focus still on its own land in suburban Arlington Heights. Capri’s group is prepared to purchase the Bears’ current Arlington Heights property, which would solve the land issue but force the team to abandon its preferred suburban setup. Chicago 4th Ward Alderman Lamont Robinson voiced strong support for the Bronzeville plan, stating it serves the community best. “I believe with everything I have, it’s the right thing for the 4th ward. And the right thing for Chicago and the bears,” Robinson said. The developers claim their plan will shape the city for generations, but the team holds the real power in the negotiation. The Clock Ticks on Illinois Newly reelected Gov. JB Pritzker intends to advance a Bears-related bill during the upcoming veto session, creating a critical moment for the stadium saga. The recent rise in developer activity suggests growing confidence that a bill could pass, even as the team keeps its Indiana option alive. The Reese option joins similar unsolicited offers made in recent weeks for sites at the former South Works steel mill and Rate Field. “We have an opportunity to make a decision that will shape Chicago for generations,” said Quintin Primo III, Capri founder and executive chairman. item.title: Bloomington South girls basketball win over North completes county sweep
item.description: Just two weeks into the season and the Bloomington South girls basketball team has vanquished it's two county rivals. The annual meeting with Bloomington North was pushed up a month earlier than in the past, with the Cougars needing to adjust their schedule as new members of the Mid-State Conference. So it was a great early-season introduction to a sectional-like atmosphere for both teams in front of a vocal crowd at South on Thursday, Nov. 12. Offense was hard to come by as the Panthers held off a second-half rally by North, getting a huge 3-pointer from freshman Quinn Wurtzman with 2:10 left in a five-point game to pull out a 48-37 win. It followed a much less rowdy 62-20 rout of Edgewood on Tuesday. More: Senior seldomly comes off field for Bloomington South football "We knew it was going to be a great crowd," North coach Kiley Jarrett said. "That's what we wanted. We wanted to simulate a playoff atmosphere and that's what it was. "I just think we just got in too big of a hole in the first half. We fought like hell to get it back within five points and a just a couple possessions here and there that made the difference." Emotions were also running high with South junior transfer Kate Lehr playing her first game against her old mates. She came out fiery to score eight of her 12 points in the first period. From there, the offense spread out among the top eight, with six scoring with five points or more. "Playing them this early, I kind of figured it would be like that," South coach Larry Winters said. "I say it often, if they'd play with the same energy against us against other teams, they'd come out with the win. They came out, 1, because Kate's here but 2, because they always play us that way. "And tonight they did a really good job because they kept our two scorers from scoring." South finished 15-of-48 shooting, hitting 5 of 16 3-pointers but also going 13-of-15 at the line. "We were trying to score more than in any other game," Winters said. "We talked about that, let the shots find you, don't try to find the shots. Tonight, we tried to find the shots. But everybody wants to show out in front of every one, so that's what happens." Winters is confident the offense will get back on track since so many have been contributing so far. "They can all score and if you're sharing the ball, that's going to happen," Winters said. "Annika (Smith) was 1-for-10 and Tatum (DeVries) took three shots. There's going to be nights like that gives an opportunity for somebody else to step up and do something. "If teams want to concentrate on a couple players when you have as many as we do, then somebody just has to step up." North digs hole in first half South (2-1) will always lean on its defense, and forcing 11 turnovers in the first half led to some easy buckets and a 29-16 lead at the break. item.description: BATTLE CREEK - Never losing a game from late August until October. Winning a conference title and a district crown. For helping his team accomplish all of that, Coldwater's Ken Delaney is the 2026 All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team Coach of the Year. The All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team is selected by nominations from the city and area coaches and voted on by the Enquirer sports staff. Along the way, Coldwater went unbeaten from August 20 until the regionals and climbed to as high as No. 12 in the Michigan Interscholastic High School Soccer Coaches rankings in Division 2. Lakeview finished as All-City Tournament champs and adds Mang Sung, Richard Lian and Cristian Duran to the team. item.title: Legendary coach Terry Waters finds new role at Fishburne
item.description: WAYNESBORO — Terry Waters is a legendary wrestling coach in the area. He was inducted into the Virginia Chapter of the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in 2022, and his photo and biographical info are in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in Stillwater, Oklahoma. Most assumed he would coach wrestling until he retired and then just walk away. Raised in a hot bed of wrestling in Pennsylvania, Waters was a student at Milton Hershey School, a boarding school for low-income families in Hershey. He and his brother were among the first Black students at the school after it integrated. Locally, Waters has coached at Staunton, Riverheads and Fort Defiance high schools, as well as at Washington & Lee University, where he was an assistant. He came to Fishburne in 2015. This past summer, he announced he was retiring from coaching. It seemed to be the end of an amazing career, but then he announced, not too longer afterward, that he would be staying at the Waynesboro school to serve as athletic director. He's now through the fall season and about to start winter sports. "It hasn't gone totally smooth, but it's been a great transition," Waters said. "The thing is I still get to coordinate a lot with the kids. That was the big decision for me, how much involvement would I get to have with the kids." He is now dealing with 20 or so coaches, not just his own assistants like he did as wrestling coach. That has been challenging. "You're dealing with 20, 24 personalities," he said. "That becomes a situation where you have to take a step back and try to understand each coach individually." Coaching for 49 years, Waters feels he had a great relationship with most of his athletic directors. He has tried to take lessons he learned from them into this job. He learned what kind of athletic director he wanted to be and what kind he didn't want to be. "I wanted to be fair, and I believe that I'm open and positive if a coach wants to talk with me," he said. "Obviously taking over a new position, you want to change some things — your approach and things like that — but overall it's gone pretty well." Fishburne offers 10 sports. Asked if he ever thought about being an athletic director, Waters took a long pause before answering. He said maybe it was in the back of his mind, but it was never something he really pursued. "When this happened, I really think it was God opening the door," Waters said. "This situation just came open." Every year, at least in recent years, someone would ask the veteran coach how much longer. His answer was always one more year. He'd talk with his wife about his future in coaching after the season ended. She would tell him if he still had the energy and the desire, he should keep coaching. "My brother pretty much summed it up when he told me if you like what you're doing, there is no sense in retiring," he said. item.title: Bulls Lose Wilson, Face Restless Hawks In NBA Cup Clash
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The Atlanta Hawks head to Chicago on Friday night with a mix of rest and frustration. The team won four of their last five games, but the recent loss to the Los Angeles Lakers still stings. Atlanta committed 20 turnovers in that game, including five in the third quarter and five more in the fourth. Coach Quin Snyder pointed out the difficulty of that situation after the game. “I know it’s hard to win when you have those lapses and you’re trying to overcome mistakes,” Snyder said, according to Yardbarker . The Hawks managed to stay close to the Lakers despite the errors, but sloppy play against a disciplined team like the Bulls could be fatal. Chicago is already struggling with a losing streak and now faces a major injury to their young star. Chicago Takes a Huge Hit The Bulls were already in a tailspin before Friday, having lost eight straight games. Their situation got much worse when rookie Caleb Wilson fractured his right hand in the third quarter against San Antonio. Wilson had been the bright spot for Chicago, averaging 18.9 points and 6.2 rebounds in his first 10 games. He also added 1.9 assists, 1.8 steals, and 0.9 blocks per game. Head coach Tiago Splitter knew the minutes were heavy for the young player before the injury occurred. Wilson was playing 30.8 minutes per night, which raised concerns about his workload. Splitter addressed the situation with a focus on long-term health rather than just immediate wins. “We’ve got to be smart with him, of course,” Splitter said. “He’s playing a lot of minutes. Those minutes are important to his development, but we’ve also got to be smart with his body being young.” Wilson will miss four to six weeks of action, leaving a massive hole in the Bulls’ rotation right before a tough matchup. Hawks Defense Steps Up While Chicago struggles, Atlanta’s defense has shown real promise. Dyson Daniels has been a force on that end, collecting four steals in the game against the Lakers. He is now averaging three steals per game, which is one more than his average from last year. Daniels explained his mindset shift in a recent interview. “I just think I’m being more aggressive on the defensive end,” Daniels said. “I feel like last year I went a little bit more passive. This year, I’m trying to be more aggressive on the ball, picking up, trying to turn people, trying to create turnovers and stuff like that.” This aggression could be the key to stopping a Bulls offense that has turned the ball over 19 times in their last loss to San Antonio. Offensively, the Hawks have reliable scorers to lean on. CJ McCollum scored 21 points off the bench and passed 17,000 career points. Nickeil Alexander-Walker also contributed 20 points, marking his fifth straight game with at least 20 points this month. The Hawks are 1-0 in the East Group C of the NBA Cup, while Chicago sits at 0-1. item.title: What does Purdue football face at Iowa? Scouting the Hawkeyes
item.description: IOWA CITY, Iowa − Two teams with different things at stake compete Saturday at Kinnick Stadium. Purdue football (3-6) seeks progress, with on-field performance needed to validate it. Iowa (7-2) still has hopes of a College Football Playoff berth. A loss to Purdue assures that won't happen. Purdue's midseason turning of the corner, complete with wins over Illinois and Minnesota, seems far more distant than one month ago. The Boilermakers need to re-establish whatever it found in those victories. Does firing defensive coordinator Kevin Kane help make inroads back to respectable defensive play? Scouting Purdue football's opponent, Iowa The Hawkeyes drew a reputation for mastering special teams and defense, but it's hard to argue with the results. Iowa has finished above .500 for 14 straights seasons and won more than 60% of its games for 12 straight. The Hawkeyes also have a offensive dynamic, ranking fifth in the Big Ten in rushing yards per game, something of a nemesis for Purdue's defense. Iowa also boasts the league's second-ranked defense and has allowed 20 total points over its past three games. Iowa statistical leaders − Passing: Hank Brown (125-190, 1,316 yards, 9 TD, 4 INT). item.description: They’re No. 1 for a reason. “The way that Coach Smart runs his program, the philosophical identity that he has in offense, defense, and special teams, the way his team plays consistently, down in and down out,” Mizzou head coach Eli Drinkwitz said Tuesday, “it's what everybody in our conference is chasing, and he does it the right way and always has done it the right way. “ … His program is the benchmark for the SEC.” Missouri football is going on the road for the final time this season this coming Saturday, when the Tigers will face top-ranked Georgia at Sanford Stadium in Athens, Georgia. The Tigers (6-3, 3-3 SEC) have made the Bulldogs (8-1, 6-1) work for their wins in the last two matchups between the teams. The Tigers had a 10-point fourth-quarter lead in 2022. Mizzou had the ball, down one score, in Athens in the fourth quarter in 2023. Both turned into UGA wins, stretching the Dawgs’ winning streak in this series to 10 straight games. Has Mizzou got a stunner in store this time around? One that could add at least a little intrigue to the final two weeks of the season in the College Football Playoff race? Here’s what Mizzou fans need to know about the Bulldogs, as well as a score prediction, for the Nov. 14 game: Georgia has SEC-best rushing success rate According to Hudl IQ’s advanced analytics, Georgia has a 61.0% rushing success rate. That statistic essentially measures how often a team stays on schedule on offense: Four or more yards on first down; 60% of the required distance on second down; 100% on third and fourth downs. No team in the SEC, per Hudl IQ, does that better than Georgia this year. Actually, only Air Force and its option offense runs the ball successfully more often in the FBS than Georgia. The Bulldogs have a by-committee approach to running the ball. Five different players have at least 100 yards on the ground this year, and four have 275 or more yards. Nate Frazier and Dwight Phillips Jr. have been the focal points of the rushing attack, but quarterback Gunner Stockton gives the Bulldogs a handy scrambling outlet with 286 sack-adjusted rushing yards this year. The most remarkable statistic: Almost exactly half of UGA’s 1,954 rushing yards this year have come before contact. That means the big fellas up front are getting consistent, significant push. For comparison, about 26% of MU’s rushing yards have been before contact, per Pro Football Focus. That all adds up to a big day ahead for the Mizzou D-line. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.title: Tom Brady Picks San Siro As The Perfect NFL Game Spot
item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Tom Brady knows what makes a crowd loud. He played in four international games during his 23-year career. He saw the noise in London and felt the heat in Mexico City. But he still thinks the best spot for an NFL game is a place that has never hosted one. Brady said he would pick San Siro in Italy if he had the power to choose. The former quarterback attended a match there in February. He watched AC Milan play Como and left with a strong feeling about the fans. “The way those Italian fans cheer all game long,” he said, according to Fox Sports . He believes the energy at that stadium is unlike anything else in the world. Brady admitted he never got to play in front of that specific crowd while he was active. A Rivalry Game Would Be Wild Brady did not just talk about the fans. He imagined what would happen if two hated rivals played there. He pictured the Cincinnati Bengals going against the Pittsburgh Steelers in that stadium. The thought of that matchup in Italy makes him smile. “That would be pretty frightening,” Brady said. He warned that a game like that would be dangerous for anyone trying to leave the building. He described the scene as a total mess. “It’d be like Mad Max escaped from LA. I’m not sure many of you guys would make it out of that stadium. It would be a complete zoo.” That is the kind of chaos the NFL needs to see more of. The league already plans to go to Munich for Week 10. At Allianz Arena, the Detroit Lions will meet the New England Patriots. The 2026 game at Allianz Arena is the only one in Germany. The League Needs To Go To Italy Brady also mentioned another spot he likes. He called Lake Como a bonus location for a future game. The stadium there is small and only holds 13,600 people. It sits right next to the water and looks beautiful. The NFL has played games in London, Melbourne, Rio de Janeiro, Paris, and Madrid this year. Mexico City will host the final international game in Week 11. The league has not yet played a game in Italy. AC Milan sits fifth in the Italian Serie A table. They have not won the league title since the 2021-22 season. Brady will not play at the San Siro after retiring, but he can still watch the sport as a fan. In Week 10, the NFL heads to Munich where the New England Patriots, once Brady’s team, play the Detroit Lions at Allianz Arena, FC Bayern Munich’s home.

item.title: Former Real Madrid defender Ivan Fresneda opens up on leaving La Fabrica: ‘Happy to have learnt so much’
item.description: Former Real Madrid defender Ivan Fresneda opens up on leaving La Fabrica: ‘Happy to have learnt so much’ Ivan Fresneda has no regrets about leaving Real Madrid’s youth academy, stating that the experience was an important part of his development. The 22-year-old Sporting CP defender discussed his journey through Spanish football in an interview with AS , reflecting on his time at La Fabrica, his memorable performance against Vinicius Jr. at the Santiago Bernabeu while playing for Real Valladolid and the growing attention surrounding his career. Now 22, Fresneda has established himself in Portugal and recently made his senior Spain debut before returning to the Under-21 squad. His progress has also brought renewed attention from major clubs, including Barcelona , who previously considered signing him when he was at Real Valladolid. Fresneda has no regrets about leaving Real Madrid Fresneda was asked whether departing Real Madrid’s academy had left him with any disappointment. His response made it clear that he views every stage of his development as valuable. Ivan Fresneda does not regret leaving Real Madrid. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) “Not at all. My time in Madrid, at Valladolid and now at Sporting has always taught me something, and I’m happy to have learnt so much and to have friends like Gonzalo – who’s here with me in the Under-21s and whom I met back then. “The truth is that you learn things at every stage, and I think I learnt a great deal from my time at La Fabrica too,” he explained. The Vinicius performance remains a career highlight One of the most memorable moments from his time in Spain came when he helped keep Vinicius quiet during a match at the Bernabeu. Asked whether that performance was the one supporters remembered most, Fresneda acknowledged its significance while pointing to his more recent achievements. “In Spain, I’d say so, but right now the one with the senior team is also up there. Barcelona had Ivan Fresneda on their radar in the past. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) “But people also remember matches with the Under-21s and at Sporting, where I provided assists and played at a very high level,” he explained. Barcelona links motivate him but Sporting are his priority As stated before, Fresneda has also attracted attention from Barcelona. The Catalan club explored his situation during his Valladolid spell, while his improved standing at Sporting has brought fresh transfer speculation. Asked how he feels about being associated with major clubs again, he responded: “I feel very proud. Having my name associated with these kinds of clubs gives me more strength and motivation to keep performing well for my club, with whom I’m under contract until 2028 and where I’m very happy,” he concluded.

item.title: Elliot Anderson was open to Man United move this summer but INEOS scuppered the deal
item.description: Elliot Anderson was open to Man United move this summer but INEOS scuppered the deal Manchester United invested over £150 million this summer to fill Casemiro’s boots, but it is safe to say that their midfield revamp has not gone according to plan. The Red Devils signed midfielders Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba to complement Kobbie Mainoo in the middle of the park. Unfortunately, none of the players have lived up to expectations, with the English giants currently languishing in 18th place in the Premier League after 10 games. United have won just one game in the league this season and are already out of the EFL Cup. Michael Carrick’s attempt to switch from the counter-attacking football that paid dividends last season, to a more controlled approach this campaign arguably cost him his job this week. Recent reports suggest that the Englishman has been let down by INEOS in the transfer market, with the Red Devils failing to sign any of his four targets. Among the players on his wish list was former Nottingham Forest midfielder Elliot Anderson, who eventually joined Manchester City this summer. United were interested in Anderson United had identified Anderson as one of their priorities for the midfield this summer but balked at Nottingham Forest’s demands. That decision has come back to haunt them, as Anderson has already established himself as a linchpin in Enzo Maresca’s setup. Anderson has featured in 15 of City’s 17 games in all competitions this season, 13 of which have been starts. The Englishman has registered one goal and two assists. Meanwhile, United have lacked tenacity and combativeness in midfield and have struggled to control games. Santos has failed to convince, and recent reports suggest that the Red Devils paid almost twice his market value. Baleba has struggled to stay fit and is expected to be sidelined for a while once again. Tielemans has been heavily involved but has not had the desired impact at the Theatre of Dreams. There remain questions over whether the £150 million INEOS invested in the trio would have been better spent on Anderson. A recent update now provides another startling insight into that pursuit that is sure to further disappoint fans. item.description: Matt Marton-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears sit pretty at 7-2 and lead the NFC North, but the road ahead looks rough. This team wins despite itself, not because of a perfect plan. A look at the numbers from Yahoo Sports shows the cracks are already showing. The offense rolls with Caleb Williams, yet the defense needs to stay sharp. One bad mistake can cost a whole game in this division. Penalties Are a Time Bomb Self-inflicted wounds are the biggest worry for this squad right now. The Bears have committed eight or more penalties in six different games this season. They dropped 12 penalties on the Carolina Panthers in Week 1 and 10 against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 8. A late foul by Zavion Thomas against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers changed the flow of that recent 27-24 win. Yahoo Sports notes that these errors could catch up to Chicago fast. The team cannot afford to be undisciplined when the schedule gets hard. Winning early masks the problem, but the math will not lie forever. The Run Game Stalls Without Monangai Chicago had the best rushing attack in the NFL through the first seven weeks, but that run ended with an injury. Kyle Monangai missed the last five games, and the ground game fell off a cliff. That number dropped to just 105 yards per game in Weeks 5-8 without him. Roschon Johnson stepped up to help, but the average is still too low for a contender. Monangai is scheduled to play in Week 11 versus the Saints, which is positive news. His return could fix the balance the offense needs to win close games. Secondary Struggles and Micah’s Take The defense has a glaring hole in the secondary that opponents will attack all year. Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love shredded this unit for 367 passing yards and two long touchdowns in Week 5. The injuries and poor play from veterans make this a major concern. Micah Parsons weighed in on the trade for Jeffery Simmons and the state of the division. On his show, “The Edge with Micah Parsons,” he said, “Adding another monster like that into the NFC North is unwarranted.” Parsons believes the AFC North is not even close to the NFC North in quality. item.title: Jameis Winston Brings Baha Men Tune To Giants Hard Count
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston tried to use a classic song to trick the Washington Commanders defense. On a fourth-and-one play near the goal line, the veteran quarterback shouted a hard count that included the lyrics to a hit from the year 2000. The move drew laughs from the broadcast booth but failed to draw a penalty from the opposing team. The Giants held a 21-17 lead with 3:41 left in the game when the moment happened. Winston wanted the Commanders to jump offsides so his team could get a fresh set of downs. He started with a standard cadence before switching to the famous tune. The play clock ran out before the snap could happen, and the Giants were forced to punt the ball away. A Viral Moment on Thursday Night Winston was playing in limited action during the Thursday night matchup. He ran two sneaks earlier in the game and gained one total yard. His hard count attempt became the most talked-about moment of the night. The video shows Winston shouting “Ready, get set, hut one, hut two, hut three!” before breaking into the song. The tune is “Who let the dogs out? Who, who, who?” according to the New York Post . This specific line has become a staple in sports culture since the Baha Men released it two decades ago. That same year, the animated movie “Rugrats in Paris: The Movie” also featured the song. Although Fox Sports observed the unorthodox tactic failed, it still generated plenty of laughs on the field. Play-by-play announcer Al Michaels chuckled at the attempt during the broadcast. Analyst Kirk Herbstreit also laughed while watching the play unfold on the field. The Commanders defense held their ground and did not jump the line. Winston remained one of the most fun personalities in the league despite the Giants losing the game. The Cost of a Gamble The failed trick play came at a high price for New York. With less than a minute left, the Commanders advanced 38 yards to score a touchdown. They took a 24-21 lead that they would not relinquish for the rest of the game. The loss dropped the Giants to a 5-3-1 record on the season. Washington improved to 3-5-1 with the win. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Even though his team lost 24-21, Winston managed to get into the highlight reel. His ability to bring joy to the game is rare for a backup quarterback. He has previously shared many press conference quotes that became viral. This hard count fits his style of being an outgoing and fun figure in the NFL. Fans across social media shared the clip widely after the game ended. The moment brought attention to the game despite the final score. Winston is making the song relevant again for a new generation of fans. The Giants will look to bounce back from this loss in their next outing.
